editorial.headline: Steel-Frame Installation: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali at Large Scale
editorial.standfirst: A specialist building-construction activity open to foreign investment nationally, with Bali’s moratorium not blocking it where large-scale OSS risk is medium-high or high.
editorial.body:
Steel-frame installation is a specialised activity within building construction: the work of installing steel frames as part of the construction work covered by a building project. The record places the activity in the steel-frame installation subclassification, KK016. Its focus is specific. This is not a general description of every task involved in making a building; it is the defined installation activity for the steel framework within that wider construction setting.

The activity is open across the full stated business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed as an activity reserved only for a particular size of enterprise. A business operating at any of those listed scales can register this activity, provided its actual work remains within the stated scope of specialised steel-frame installation as part of building construction.

Nationally, the PMA position is direct: the activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment may hold the full ownership stake permitted by that national ceiling. The governing PMA references in the record are Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap recorded here, so the national picture is one of full foreign-investment openness rather than partial access.

Bali does not overturn that national position for this activity. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That risk position means the activity is not blocked by Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The distinction is important: Bali’s moratorium remains a real provincial rule, but this activity is recorded as outside its block at the stated large-scale risk level. For a foreign investor considering steel-frame installation in Bali, the honest conclusion is that the activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not blocked by that Bali moratorium on the record’s stated basis.
